title: Ask Comet about the page beside it
summary: Comet is a browser with a helper at the side. Check whether the helper read the tab you meant.
where: On a computer visit perplexity.ai/comet. On iPad follow the official app link. Use a page with public practice text.

actions.title: Open Comet
actions.do: Install the official browser for your device and open it. You can leave your bookmarks where they are.
actions.see: You see a browser window with an address box.
actions.stuck: If you opened a regular Perplexity search page in Safari, switch to the Comet app.

actions.title: Choose a page
actions.do: Enter example.com. Read the heading at the top.
actions.see: The page says Example Domain.
actions.stuck: If you only see search results, put https://example.com in the address box.

actions.title: Ask the side helper
actions.do: Open Assistant and ask for the current page heading and its web address. Read the result beside the page.
actions.see: The heading matches, and the address is example.com.
actions.stuck: If it describes another site, select the tab with the practice page again.

actions.title: Change tabs
actions.do: Open example.org. Ask for the heading and address again. Look closely at the end of the address.
actions.see: The two headings match. The second address ends in .org.
actions.stuck: A matching heading alone cannot prove which tab the helper read.

roles: Read a public mail help page.
Check a fact in a public Teams guide.
Compare help pages for two app features.

title: Follow a search answer back to its source
summary: Perplexity puts links beside its answers. Check one small fact before you use it.
where: Open perplexity.ai in Safari or another browser. Use a regular search. This practice uses a public space mission.

actions.title: Ask one question
actions.do: Ask: When did Apollo 11 launch? Link to the space agency’s own mission page.
actions.see: Look for a date with a source link beside it.
actions.stuck: If the answer lists many missions, narrow the question to Apollo 11.

actions.title: Open the evidence
actions.do: Tap the link beside the date. Read the publisher name and find the launch date on that page.
actions.see: The mission launched on July 16, 1969.
actions.stuck: If you landed on a general home page, look for the mission page and its launch section.

actions.title: Ask a second question
actions.do: Ask when the lunar module landed on the Moon. Write the launch and landing dates on separate lines.
actions.see: The landing took place on July 20, 1969. It is a different event.
actions.stuck: If the answer gives the date of a Moon walk, ask specifically for the landing.

actions.title: Check your two lines
actions.do: Reopen the source. Label the two dates Launch and Landing. Count the calendar days between them.
actions.see: The dates are four days apart. Each label points to the right event.
actions.stuck: If the dates are reversed, check which event came first.

roles: Check a fact in a public mail guide.
Find the original release note for a work tool.
Check the answer key for a space quiz.

title: Give Grok Bot a file you can check
summary: Make a two-row table. Then see whether the file matches the reply.
where: Visit x.ai/bot on a computer for the official app. Use an account with Bot access. You can write the same table on paper.

actions.title: Open the app
actions.do: Install the version for your device. Choose Sign in. When the browser finishes, return to the Bot app.
actions.see: You can see a list of bots or a control to add one.
actions.stuck: Check that you opened the Bot app if you only see a normal chat.

actions.title: Choose a job
actions.do: Use New Bot or the plus sign in the side menu. Call it List Helper. Use a fresh practice folder if asked.
actions.see: You have one place for the table job.
actions.stuck: If you cannot add a bot with your account, use a practice chat to try the table request.

actions.title: Make a small CSV
actions.do: Ask for fruit.csv. Give it columns Fruit and Count. Use plum 2 and pear 3. Ask for a file with no extra rows.
actions.see: A CSV is plain text. Commas separate the two columns.
actions.stuck: If the reply just prints the rows, ask for the file as well.

actions.title: Read the saved file
actions.do: Open fruit.csv and read both counts. Add them yourself. Compare with the helper’s total if it gave one.
actions.see: Two rows, two kinds of fruit, five pieces in all.
actions.stuck: If the total is added as a third fruit, ask it to keep the total in the message instead.

roles: Count rows in a fake mail table.
Check a file your app saves.
sources: xAI · sign in and make a Bot

title: Have Mistral Vibe draft a checklist
summary: Turn two short notes into two boxes you could tick.
where: Open chat.mistral.ai. Sign in if your account supports it. Older guides may call the app Le Chat.

actions.title: Open a new task
actions.do: Pick Work in the side menu if it appears. Otherwise start a fresh chat for the sample.
actions.see: You see a blank place to type.
actions.stuck: If you are in an older thread, open a new one so its list cannot get mixed in.

actions.title: Give two facts
actions.do: Type: Carry the game box. Charge the phone. Make a checklist using only those two jobs.
actions.see: The reply includes both jobs.
actions.stuck: If it adds travel supplies, repeat only the two sentences and ask for two items.

actions.title: Set the shape
actions.do: Ask for one empty box at the start of each line. Use five words or fewer in each line.
actions.see: There are two short lines, each with a box.
actions.stuck: If the second line is long, count its words and ask for a shorter version.

actions.title: Make one edit
actions.do: Ask to replace phone with tablet. Keep the first job exactly the same.
actions.see: The game box is still first. The second line now says tablet.
actions.stuck: Compare the first line with the earlier version before keeping the edit.

roles: Turn a mail check into a short list.
Draft short labels for a checklist app.
sources: Mistral · Le Chat is now Vibe

title: Make a short video from a still picture
summary: Does a mug keep its shape as the camera moves? Make one small clip and find out.
where: Use firefly.adobe.com on a computer. Start with a photo of a mug on a plain table. Check your available video credits before you generate.

actions.title: Find the video tool
actions.do: Choose Video, then Generate video. Find the control for the first frame, which is the opening picture.
actions.see: There is a place to add a start image.
actions.stuck: If the screen asks for an image prompt only, switch from Image to Video.

actions.title: Set the first frame
actions.do: Add the mug photo under Frames. Leave the final frame empty for this test.
actions.see: A small copy of the mug appears as the first frame.
actions.stuck: Remove a wrong photo before you generate the clip.

actions.title: Ask for one motion
actions.do: Type: Move slowly closer to the mug. Keep it still on the table. Generate one short clip if your plan allows it.
actions.see: A preview appears when the clip is ready.
actions.stuck: If video is unavailable, draw a wide view and a close view on paper and compare the mug.

actions.title: Watch twice
actions.do: First watch the camera move. Play it again and watch the handle. Does it stay attached on the same side?
actions.see: A usable clip moves closer without changing the mug’s shape.
actions.stuck: If the handle bends, try less motion and a simpler background.

roles: Show one step in a mail help clip.
Make a training slide with a short clip.
Test motion for an app preview.

title: Put a toy boat beside a mug
summary: Tell Firefly exactly which small patch of a photo it may change.
where: Open Adobe Firefly with a photo of a mug on an empty table. On mobile, choose Generative fill and upload the photo.

actions.title: Open the photo
actions.do: On the web choose Image, then Edit image. Pick your photo. Choose Fill in the edit tools.
actions.see: The mug and table are visible with a brush control.
actions.stuck: If you see only a text box, open the image editor first.

actions.title: Mark the patch
actions.do: Brush over a small patch beside the mug. Leave the mug and handle outside your mark.
actions.see: A colored patch shows the space you chose.
actions.stuck: Use Select less or subtract if the mark touches the mug.

actions.title: Add the boat
actions.do: Type: a small orange toy sailboat sitting on the table. Choose Fill or Generate. Look at one result.
actions.see: The boat should sit on the tabletop inside the patch.
actions.stuck: If it floats, move the patch down to include the boat and table in the same view.

actions.title: Check what stayed
actions.do: Compare both photos. Look at the handle, the table edge and the shadow. Save the edited picture as a new copy.
actions.see: You can point to the added boat. The original picture is still yours.
actions.stuck: If the mug changed, start from the first photo with a smaller patch.

roles: Polish a made-up picture for a mail guide.
Add a prop in a practice training slide.
Try a new object on a game cover.
sources: Adobe · Generative Fill on the web
